blocks.content:
Every High Court is a Court of Record.

Meaning:
• Its judgments are permanent records
• It can punish for contempt of court
Every High Court is a Court of Record.

items: Questions frequently ask under which Constitutional Article the High Court is declared a 'Court of Record' (Article 215).
Examiners often test the two main powers of a Court of Record: keeping permanent legal records and punishing for contempt of court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 215 establishes that every High Court in India is a Court of Record.
The judgments, proceedings, and acts of a High Court are preserved as permanent records.
A Court of Record has the inherent judicial power to punish for contempt of court.
